Q: Make a program in which the user introduces the lenght value of the radius or side of a shape, then selects a shape, which is drawn with said value? A:

The root issue is using texto.get() rather than Entry.get(1.0, "end-1c").

Beyond that, I'd suggest combining the turtle window as part of the tkinter window, as follows:

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import ttk, messagebox
from turtle import RawTurtle, TurtleScreen

root = tk.Tk()
root.geometry("600x500")
root.title("Dibujos de figuras")

control_frame = tk.Frame(root)
control_frame.pack(side=tk.TOP, fill=tk.X, pady=10)

tk.Label(control_frame, text="Radio o lado en cm:").pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)

size_entry = tk.Entry(control_frame, font="Helvetica 15", width=10)
size_entry.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)

figure_var = tk.StringVar()
figure_combobox = ttk.Combobox(
    control_frame,
    state="readonly",
    textvariable=figure_var,
    values=["Círculo", "Cuadrado", "Triángulo", "Pentágono", "Hexágono"],
)
figure_combobox.current(0)
figure_combobox.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)

canvas_frame = tk.Frame(root)
canvas_frame.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)

canvas = tk.Canvas(canvas_frame, width=600, height=400, bg="white")
canvas.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)

screen = TurtleScreen(canvas)
t = RawTurtle(screen)
t.hideturtle()
t.speed(0)


def generate_figure():
    t.clear()
    size_str = size_entry.get()
    if not size_str:
        messagebox.showerror("Error", "Invalid number")
        return

    try:
        size = float(size_str)
    except ValueError:
        messagebox.showerror("Error", "Invalid number")
        return

    figura = figure_var.get()

    if figura == "Círculo":
        t.circle(size)
    elif figura == "Cuadrado":
        for _ in range(4):
            t.forward(size)
            t.right(90)
    elif figura == "Triángulo":
        for _ in range(3):
            t.forward(size)
            t.right(120)
    elif figura == "Pentágono":
        for _ in range(5):
            t.forward(size)
            t.right(72)
    elif figura == "Hexágono":
        for _ in range(6):
            t.forward(size)
            t.right(60)


generate_button = tk.Button(control_frame, text="Generate", command=generate_figure)
generate_button.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=10)
root.mainloop()

You can modify/extend this from here to fulfill your exact requirements.

Q: How to execute command from one docker container to another A:

I had the same issue but i didn't want to expose the docker socket, also setting up ssh for this is a bit overkill in my opinion. I decided to use redis streams for this as i already had a redis container in the same network.

container 1 adds an entry to the stream and container 2 which is listening for it, picks it up and executes the job. i personally used python but it can be done with other languages or just pure bash.

Run in Container 2

import contextlib
import logging
import subprocess
import time

import redis

STREAM = "jobs"
GROUP = "workers"
CONSUMER = "worker-1"

TASKS = {
    "run_hc_cv": ["echo 'foo $(date)' >> /tmp/t.log"],
    # "reload": ["/app/reload.sh"],
}

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)


def redis_job_runner() -> None:
    rdb = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

    with contextlib.suppress(redis.ResponseError):
        rdb.xgroup_create(STREAM, GROUP, id="$", mkstream=True)

    logger.info("Worker started")
    while True:
        entries = rdb.xreadgroup(
            groupname=GROUP,
            consumername=CONSUMER,
            streams={STREAM: ">"},
            count=1,
            block=5000,
        )

        if not entries:
            continue

        _, messages = entries[0]

        for msg_id, data in messages:
            task = data.get("task")

            cmd = TASKS.get(task)
            if not cmd:
                rdb.xack(STREAM, GROUP, msg_id)
                continue

            try:
                subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, shell=True)
                rdb.xack(STREAM, GROUP, msg_id)
                logger.info("%s task completed: %s", task, msg_id)
            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
                logger.warning("%s task failed", task)
                # leave unacked for retry
                time.sleep(2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    redis_job_runner()

Send Job in Container 1


rdb = redis.Redis()

stream = "jobs"
task = "run_hc_cv"
rdb.xadd(stream, {"task": task})

print(f"Queued task: {task}")
